I Want to Be Yours and Other Songs
I Want to Be Yours and Other Songs album cover by Havre De Grace

An accidental debut album originally released under the moniker *Stefan Auvache*. Eight songs written and recorded for Stefan to listen to personally, eventually compiled, mixed, and released in 2025. The album was rereleased under the name *Havre De Grace* in January 2026.

Everyone belongs to somebody — I want to be yours.

This album came about by accident. I had been playing guitar and writing songs for years. As the songs slowly got better and better, I decided to record a couple of them. Fast forward a year, and a friend of mine reached out to me about recording something in an actual studio. Fast forward another year, and I had 4-5 songs recorded. I reached out to that same friend, recorded a few more songs, and sent them off to him for some proper mixing. The result is this album — I Want to Be Yours and Other Songs.

While a few of the tracks developed over years of playing and changes, most of them were written in less than ten minutes. I would have a riff in my hand and a thought would pop into my head. A few minutes later, I would have the words to a new song. A few of the songs (including the title track) were written during my first few months of fatherhood. Other songs are about stories I heard as a kid, the struggle to write and perform music, and thoughts that have been on my mind for a long time.

I had such a great time putting this album together.

I hope you enjoy it.

I was rocking and humming my 3-month-old son to sleep at 2am. When he finally passed out, I laid him between my legs and the line "yes I could be famous, that'd sure be a chore. I could belong to anybody but I want to be yours" popped into my head. Less than five minutes later, all of the words were written as they are now.

This was the first song I intentionally recorded for the album. Everything else up to this point had been randomly recorded over the past few years. This was the real beginning of forming the album (hence the title).

I remember a story my mom told me when I was a kid about a guy in our hometown. His wife left him and their two kids to travel cross country with a motorcycle gang for a year. When she eventually came back and asked for forgiveness, he welcomed her back with open arms. I don't know if that story is true or exaggerated or spot on accurate, but I do know how it makes me feel. Shades of Blue and Red is about that story.
This was originally a demo I recorded two years before deciding to record the rest of the album. I had some time off work, bought a couple of SM57 mics, and recorded some songs.
